todo: Purpose: Compose the maglev’s crossing over the Lull gorge as a unique long-range landmark.
Visual brief: Three supported masonry/iron piers at the actual gorge section, high horizontal guideway, narrow dark undersides and a clear river opening; visible cliffs carry the bridge abutments.
Implement after review: Claude selects the design, draws it, supplies exact anchors/collision and passes the library gate; no concept may ship.
Geometry: proposed authoring envelope 32x14 cells; one cell is 8 world px / 24 art px. This is not an asserted solid footprint; collision, foot and overhang await the drawing.
Scale: envelope only, not the viaduct’s canonical dimensions or a collision box; actual plan/section controls the span.
Rule proposal: piers sit on mapped support, abutments meet the correct transport tier, and river flow passes through an unobstructed opening.
Uniqueness: rail and pier details are shared but the three-pier gorge silhouette is not stamped elsewhere; W7 transport access remains owner-controlled.
